entries.test: A collapse of the generative AI sector, demonstrated by widespread business failures and a sustained collapse in investment, would test the eventual-collapse commitment.
entries.note: The sentence mixes evaluative language with a firm, undated prediction of collapse.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures showing whether generative AI businesses earned profits at publication would test the factual premise.
entries.note: Context makes 'making money' a claim about profit. His nearby NVIDIA exception complicates the absolute wording.

entries.test: Inflation-adjusted historical AWS buildout expenditures compared with Amazon's 2024 and 2025 capital expenditures would test the cost comparison.
entries.note: 'A bargain' is evaluative, but the relative expenditure claim is factual.
He judges the comparison inappropriate without specifying a factual equivalence to test.
The feature-versus-infrastructure distinction has no shared operational boundary here.

entries.test: Public pricing agreements, customer expenditure reports, and model operating-cost disclosures would test whether increased customer charges offset rising model costs.
entries.note: The steroid metaphor accompanies a concrete economic mechanism. 'I believe' does not by itself make this a probability claim.
The pricing forecast explicitly says 'highly unlikely.' The separate assertion that no enterprise AI startup is profitable is checkable.
There is no agreed subscriber-growth threshold that makes a business intrinsically worth $300 billion.

entries.test: Public financial results and documented unit economics would show whether Perplexity has a financially viable route to profitability.
entries.note: The profitability assertion has a plain financial reading; 'not anything new' is a broader characterization.
'Out of ideas' supplies no shared standard for novelty or hypergrowth potential.
The statement about what users of 'agent' mean is explicitly qualified by 'likely.' The separate product-autonomy assertion can be tested through documented capabilities.

entries.test: Public financial statements or credible financial reporting would establish whether each company was losing billions of dollars annually at publication.
entries.note: The quantified losses are checkable. The historical analogy lacks a precise similarity standard.

entries.test: Public cash-flow figures, financing requirements, infrastructure commitments, and unit economics would test the claimed dependence on continuing outside capital.
entries.note: This asserts present financial dependence and lack of a viable profitability route.

entries.test: Anthropic's public pricing and usage-limit history, customer revenue breakdowns, and financial reporting would test the stated prices, customer ranking, costs, and profitability prospects.
entries.note: 'Desperate' is an evaluative gloss on several concrete factual assertions.
'Absolutely horrifying business' is a judgment of worth without a specified financial threshold.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures or credible reporting identifying a profitable generative AI coding or search company at publication would refute the profitability assertion.
entries.note: 'Not real businesses' is evaluative; the assertion that none are profitable is testable.
The offered justification depends on a counterfactual stock market in which AI earnings determine prices.
'Terrible' and 'worse' rank business quality without a shared measure.
Neither 'really innovative' nor the degree of difficulty has a shared test in this formulation.

entries.test: Following a documented change in Microsoft's OpenAI-related investment, NVIDIA's sales disclosures and Microsoft procurement records would show whether its revenue was affected.
entries.note: The prediction is conditional and has no deadline.

entries.test: Public measurements of inference resource use and operating costs for larger and smaller models under comparable workloads would test the asserted cost relationship.
entries.note: The possibility concession does not weaken his firm assertion about the evidence. API prices alone would not establish operating costs.

entries.test: Public market concentration data, major customers' GPU purchases, and financial returns on installed AI infrastructure would test the claimed market dependence and losses.
entries.note: The historical brittleness ranking is imprecise, but the market-dependence and immediate-loss assertions are factual.
